mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average for at least 3 consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return tends to be positive due to lower real borrowing costs and increased equity discounting.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < mean(FEDFUNDS) over the past 12 months for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, SPX 20-day returns are not statistically different from the prior 20-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in unemployment (UNRATE) predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days as labor market strength boosts investor confidence.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 2% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by at least 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: Across 10 consecutive such labor-market events, cumulative 5-day SPX returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average for two consecutive months is associated with a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days as it signals robust economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > INDPRO_12MA for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 20 such events, the 60-day SPX forward return is not significantly higher than the 60-day risk-free return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly exceeds 2% in a given month, the S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days tends to be negative due to market anticipation of tighter monetary policy and higher real rates.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 200 for any month (where 200 is the 2023 Q1 monthly value as reference)
failure_condition: Over 10 such episodes, the 20-day SPX return is not statistically lower than the 20-day Treasury bill return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in housing starts (HOUST) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) creates a dual signal of demand and liquidity, predicting a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by at least 10% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by at least 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: Across 5 such events, the 20-day SPX return is not significantly higher than the 20-day risk-free rate (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in job openings (PAYEMS) accompanied by a steady unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% suggests a softening labor market, which tends to produce a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases by at least 5% month-over-month for three consecutive months while UNRATE < 4%
failure_condition: In 8 such episodes, the 60-day SPX return is not statistically lower than the 60-day risk-free return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly rise in retail sales (not available in provided proxies; fallback to GDPC1 as proxy for aggregate demand) and a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates shifting consumption versus investment demand, predicting a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by at least 2% month-over-month while INDPRO decreases by at least 1% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Across 4 such events, the 5-day SPX return is not significantly lower than the 5-day Treasury bill return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month moving average of real GDP deflator (not directly available; fallback to CPIAUCSL) shows a sharp decline without a corresponding drop in industrial production (INDPRO), it suggests supply-side easing and predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by at least 1% month-over-month for two consecutive months while INDPRO remains flat or increases
failure_condition: In 6 such episodes, the 20-day SPX return is not significantly higher than the 20-day risk-free rate (t-test p > 0.05).
